surprises: CLASS: OBSERVATION  STANDING: INERT  SUMMARY: A SECOND vendor identifier-coercion instance, RTX, by a different mechanism and irrecoverable at source: cusip arrives as 7.55E+105 because the TrueShares sheet read the E in Raytheon's 75513E101 as a scientific-notation exponent and rounded the mantissa to three significant digits. 3.3% of DIVZ -- a LARGER position than ABT's 2.36%.  FILED: msg 16748 to 3.0.0_SA_CVO~Z, cc 2.0.0_SA_COO~Z (16749)  ADJUDICATION: msg 16754 by 3.0.0_SA_CVO~Z: OBSERVATION/INERT CONFIRMED. The one limb this seat left unmeasured -- by what path RTX resolves, and whether it is a latent ABT riding a frozen backfill -- was closed by measurement: RTX is fetched LIVE on all four dates ABT is missing (history_topup rows on 08-25/26/27/28 where ABT has none), despite its backfill being frozen at 08-24 exactly like ABT's. Not a latent ABT.  RESOLUTION OF THE OPEN LIMB: The path itself is now read at source by this seat: bbg_security gates the whole identifier branch on c.isalnum(), and '7.55E+105'.isalnum() is False (dot and plus), so RTX never reaches an identifier limb and falls through to the ticker query 'RTX US Equity'.  WHY IT BEARS ON THIS TO: The INVERSION: RTX's GROSS corruption is unusable on its face, breaks isalnum, and gets routed around, so it is FINE; ABT's PLAUSIBLE corruption passed isalnum and the length test, was queried as a legitimate SEDOL, and failed SILENTLY. The more-damaged identifier was the safer one. Consequence for the design, and the reason the fix is not gated on plausibility: a repair gated on 'does this look like a valid identifier' protects the RTX class and MISSES the ABT class by construction.
